excerpt: safetyStopNavigation("planner backend PVA command anchor is not near vehicle");
claim: 14 of 16 PAUSED_SAFETY_STOP stops are raised by the adapter tracking envelope (stage TRACKING_ENVELOPE, kCommandAnchorErrorLimitM = 0.75 m, command_safety_contract.hpp:10) on a brake command: role EMERGENCY in 13, BACKUP in 1. The envelope metric is 0.751-0.794 m in 13 of 14 (0.893 m in the other), i.e. 0.001-0.044 m above the limit; the vehicle is ahead of the command along its travel in all 14 (0.70-0.88 m projected on the velocity direction). The runtime independently rejects the planned STOPPED_HOLD endpoint against the same 0.75 m (navigation_runtime_node.cpp:9089-9110) in 15 of 16 runs (0.753-1.579 m). Two stops are decided by the runtime latch alone (run 10: STOPPED_HOLD endpoint 0.753 m vs 0.750 m, adapter then reports command stale; run 14: PlanFromRest recovery timeout 5.0 s).
failure_scenario: Any renewal failure at cruise speed ends in a hard measured-state brake that the vehicle overshoots by about the envelope size; the mission is abandoned (PX4 Hold) although the vehicle is inside the free corridor. FAST profiles at 5-8 m/s (F1/F2) inherit this with larger brake distances.
direction: Measure vehicle-minus-command end-of-brake error versus entry speed and role on SITL before any design decision (distribution first, AGENTS.md); architect decides whether the brake profile, the envelope or the hand-over policy changes. No threshold proposed here.

claim: A failed renewal solve becomes the one-shot measured-state emergency brake whenever the retained command is beyond the retained tracking limit (0.25 m = planner.yaml:65 tracking_error_budget_m, via retainedCommandTrackingLimit) AND the MAIN phase bridge is not usable (tracking_certificate_exceeded = !phase_execution_bridge_usable && ...; the bridge needs path_relative_tracking_accepted with |phase offset| <= kMainTrackingPhaseWindowS = 0.10 s, command_safety_contract.hpp:16). Over the 147 failing solves of the 18 M1 sessions with a measured anchor error: bridge unavailable and anchor above 0.25 m -> emergency committed in 70 of 70 (37 of 37 without run 14, whose 33 are a PlanFromRest hold loop); bridge usable -> emergency in 0 of 33 (12 of them with anchor above 0.25 m, 0.45-0.55 m, e.g. run 5 at 5 m/s, phase offset -0.09 s accepted); 25 solves have no measured anchor error. In 13 of 16 stopped runs the head of the final failing streak is exactly this case (bridge unavailable, anchor 0.27-0.65 m, emergency in the same record) and the adapter stop follows 0.5-0.9 s later. Path-relative phase offsets recorded at speed >= 4.5 m/s are -0.075 to -0.10 s (median -0.080 s; values are carried over between solves, indicative only), i.e. the steady lag of the vehicle behind the timed command at 5 m/s is of the size of the 0.10 s window and the raw anchor error (median 0.48 m) is about twice the 0.25 m limit.
failure_scenario: Cruise at 5 m/s is only as robust as the path-relative bridge: any renewal failure while the bridge is rejected or unavailable becomes a hard brake (T1-02) and a mission abort. The same 0.25 m is the planner robot-radius padding (config.hpp:256), so it cannot be widened without touching the obstacle margin.
direction: Add per-cycle anchor error to execution_diagnostics (T1-06) and measure the anchor-error distribution during successful cruise at 3/5 m/s before judging whether 0.25 m is reachable in steady tracking; behavior options belong to the architect (ADR-020 W3/W5 neighbourhood).

claim: classifyPlannerFailure maps every PLANNER_CANDIDATE_REJECTED (-7) to commit_recertification/world_changed. In the 20 sessions 44 solves carry that label: 32 are MAIN route-regression certificate rejections, 4 are latest-WorldModel tube blocked (cell OCCUPIED), 8 are commit-gate kWorldAdvanced (matched one-to-one by order with the planner WARN lines in logs/mapping.log, counts equal in 20/20 sessions). planner_trace stage/reason therefore over-attribute 36 of 44 rejections to a world change.

direction: Observability-only commit: distinct failure reasons for route-regression, latest-world certificate and commit-gate rejections (no behavior change).
